# CHRONICLE

...she turned the sea into dry land. When the Roman people learned of the tyrannical rule of the Egyptians and **Cleopatra**, **Antony** <note>The Greek text says "Antony" (Antonius), but the Latin translation and historical context suggest "Augustus" (Octavian) is intended here as the one leading the Roman response.</note> set out from Rome, fully armed against Cleopatra, the Egyptians, and the regions of Persia, because they were disturbing the peace of the East.

<margin>V 154</margin> It is recorded that during these times a certain **Sosibius of Antioch**, a man of <term>Senatorial rank</term><note>A member of the Roman Senate, the highest social and political class in Rome.</note>, went up to Rome with **Augustus**. <margin>5</margin> At the time of his death, he left his entire income to his home city <note>Antioch</note> on the condition that every five years, for the full thirty days of the month of **Peritios** <note>A month in the Macedonian calendar used in the East, roughly corresponding to February.</note>, games should be held there. <margin>B</margin> These were to include <term>acroamatic</term> <note>Musical or poetic recitations.</note>, <term>thymelic</term> <note>Performances centered around the altar in a theater, such as choral singing.</note>, and stage performances, as well as athletic contests <margin>10</margin> and horse racing.

It is said that **Augustus** was the first to become the sole monarch of the Romans, and he was officially titled as follows: **Augustus Caesar Octavianus, Triumphator, Augustus** <note>The Revered</note>, **Mighty, Imperator**—which means "Supreme Commander" or "Autocrat."

When Augustus arrived in Egypt, he took control of the land <margin>15</margin> and brought down the kingdom of the **Ptolemies**, which had endured for 296 years. <margin>C</margin>

**Augustus Octavian** ruled as sole monarch for 44 years. The total number of years <note>since the creation of the world</note> was 5,521.

**3rd Indiction.** <note>A 15-year tax and dating cycle.</note> **13th year.** **Consuls: Octavian Augustus (for the 8th time) and Taurus.**

Once the Romans accepted the challenge of the tyranny of the Egyptians and Cleopatra, Augustus set out from Rome, having gathered and led out his forces against Cleopatra, the Egyptians, and the Persian coasts, because they were troubling the East.

Sosibius, in this same season, an Antiochian of the Senatorial order, is reported to have come to Rome with Augustus; upon dying, he left all his revenues to his fatherland on this condition: that every five years, for the thirty days of the month of Peritios, Recitation, Thymelic, Stage, and Athletic games, and even Equestrian games, should be celebrated there.

# CHRONICLE

### 194th Olympiad.

<margin>C</margin> **Indiction 14. Year 39. Under the 14th Consulship of Octavian Augustus and Silanus.** <note>The Roman "Consulship" was used to date years; this corresponds to roughly 2 BCE.</note>

**In this year 5596 from the creation of the world, after the completion of the 26th year of Augustus Caesar’s monarchy and the sixth month—that is, during the 39th year of his reign—we wish** <margin>5</margin>
**to determine the lunar age on the first day of the seventh month, Elul** <note>Elul is the sixth month of the civil year and the twelfth month of the ecclesiastical year in the Hebrew calendar, here equated with September.</note>, **according to the lunar tradition of Scripture, and to find which day of the week it falls upon. Subtracting 1 year from the 5596 years, we take 5595 and divide by 19** <note>The "19-year cycle" or Metonic cycle is used to align the solar year with lunar phases.</note>. **19 times 200 is 3800; 19 times 80 is 1520; 19 times 9 is 171. The remainder is 14.** <margin>V 156 D 10</margin>
**The 14th year of the <term>19-year cycle</term> <note>original: "ἐννεακαιδεκαετηρίδος" (enneakaidekaeteridos)</note> has 4 <term>epacts</term> <note>Epacts are the number of days by which the solar year exceeds the lunar year, used to determine the age of the moon.</note>. To these we add 13 days from before the luminaries and 11 days starting from March 21. Adding the days of the months: April (30), May (31), June (30), July (31), August (31), and September 1, the total is 182. Divide this by thirty, and the remainder is 2. We have therefore learned that in this present year 5596 from the creation of the world, the 1st solar day** <margin>15</margin>
**of the month of September fell on the 2nd day of the moon.**

**Next, let us determine on which day of the week the first of September fell. To the 5595 years we add a fourth part** <note>This "fourth part" (1398) accounts for leap years in the Julian system.</note>, **specifically 1398, which produces 6993.** <margin>P 195</margin>
**Divide this total by 7. 7 times 900 is 6300; 7 times 80 is 560; 7...**

Now let us work by 19: multiply 19 by 200, it makes 3800; multiply 19 by 80, there are 1520; multiply 19 by 9, 171 are produced; the remainder will be 14. The fourteenth year of the nineteen-year cycle has 4 Epacts. To these we add 13 before the luminaries, and those 11 from March 21: April (30), May (31), June (30), July (31), August (31), and September 1, which makes 182. Remove the blocks of thirty, and 2 are left. We have understood, therefore, that in this present year of the world 5596, the first solar day of the month of September fell on the second moon.**

**Then let us also see on which day of the week the first day of September occurred. To 5595 we add the fourth part, namely 1398, and 6993 is produced. Let us divide this whole amount by 7. 7 multiplied by 900 makes...**

### CHRONICON

On the fifth day of the week, the holy Mother of God <term>Theotokos (God-bearer)</term> went into the hill country to Elizabeth and greeted her. Under the consulship of Lentulus and Piso. <note>Gnaeus Cornelius Lentulus and Marcus Valerius Messalla Messallinus (often identified as "Piso" in this tradition) were Roman consuls in 3 BC.</note> Tebeth 31 days of January, Shevat 28 days of February, Adar 25 days of March. Together, these make 183 days. Divide these according to the lunar cycle: <margin>5</margin> 6 times 20 makes 120; 6 times 10 makes 60; that is, the half of 6 makes 3. <note>The author is using a base-6 calculation to demonstrate how these 183 days align with lunar patterns to prove the precision of the biblical timeline.</note>

In this 5507th year <note>counting from the creation of the world according to the Byzantine era</note>, the Annunciation of the conception of our Lord Jesus Christ, the true God, was given to our Lady the Mother of God on the 25th of the month of March, on the second day of the week.

<margin>V 159</margin> In this 5507th year of the creation of the world, on the 15th day of the 7th month, during the days of the Feast of Tabernacles <note>original: "σκηνοπηγιῶν" (skēnōpēgiōn)</note>, Zechariah—being in the presence of God—received the good news of the <margin>10</margin> conception of Elizabeth.

<margin>P 198</margin> Therefore, on the 25th of the month of Dystros <note>Dystros is the Macedonian name for the month of March.</note>, the six-month period of Elizabeth’s pregnancy was completed. For this reason, the Evangelist says: "In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Na-<margin>15</margin>zareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house and lineage of David; and the virgin’s name was Mary. And the an-<margin>20</margin>gel said to her, 'Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God...'" <note>A quotation from the Gospel of Luke 1:26-30.</note>

...at the voice of the angel speaking to the holy Virgin: *The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the holy child to be born will be called the Son of God.* <note>original: Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σὲ...; quoting Luke 1:35.</note> On the same second day of creation in which Christ our God made the heavens, He is found to have taken flesh and become fully human, existing as the <term>Sun of Righteousness<note>original: ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης (hēlios dikaiosynēs); a title for Christ drawn from the prophecy of Malachi, suggesting he brings spiritual light and life to the world.</note></term>. For in this present year 5507, it is the 16th year of the <term>nineteen-year cycle<note>Also known as the Metonic cycle; a period of 19 years after which the phases of the moon recur on the same days of the solar year, used to calculate the date of Easter.</note></term>, <margin>15</margin> and it has 15 recorded <term>epacts<note>original: ἐπακτὰς (epaktas); the age of the moon in days on January 1st, used to determine the lunar calendar for the year.</note></term>. To these we add the 13 days before the luminaries, 7 pre-lunar days, and 5 days starting from March 21st; the total is 40. Subtract 30, and 10 remain.

And we recognize how the tenth day of the first lunar month <margin>D</margin> <margin>20</margin> was found in this present year to be on the twenty-fifth of the month of March according to the Romans.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Presentation of Christ in the Temple, specifically focusing on the prophecy of Simeon. <page-num>883</page-num>
# PASCHALE

...[not] complex nor deep. <margin>5</margin> For Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother: "Behold, this child is set for the fall and resurrection of many in Israel, and for a sign that shall be spoken against. And a sword shall pierce your own soul also." <note>This is the famous prophecy of Simeon from Luke 2:34–35, often called the "Sword of Sorrows."</note> Yet to me it seems no less difficult to understand how the same person is set for both fall and resurrection, and what the "sign spoken against" is, and thirdly, how a sword shall pierce the soul of Mary. I believe, <margin>P 204</margin> therefore, that the Lord is for fall and resurrection not in the sense of some people falling and others rising, but rather that which is worse in us falls while that which is better is raised up. <margin>10</margin> For the appearance of the Lord is destructive of bodily passions but restorative to the distinct qualities of the soul. Just as when Paul says, "When I am weak, then I am strong," <note>2 Corinthians 12:10</note> the same man is both weak and strong—but he is weak in the flesh and strong in the spirit. <margin>15</margin> So also the Lord does not provide the occasion for falling to some and rising to others; for those who fall clearly fall from a position in which they once stood. <margin>B</margin> But the unbeliever never stands; he is always dragged along, creeping with the serpent. <note>A reference to the serpent in Eden, representing the low, earthly nature of sin.</note> Therefore, he has no place from which to fall, because he is already cast down by his unbelief. The first <margin>V 164</margin> <margin>20</margin> blessing for one standing in sin is to fall and die <note>To "die to sin" is a common New Testament theme, meaning to stop living according to worldly desires.</note>, then to live in righteousness and be raised up through the knowledge of Christ.

Line 13: Reference to 2 Corinthians 12:10. Line 17: Manuscript P uses 'had stood.' Line 18: Manuscript P uses 'creeps along.' Line 20: Manuscript P reads 'blessing for those standing.'</note>

### **From Basil the Great.**

Simeon’s words to Mary are neither complex nor deep. For Simeon blessed her and said to Mary his mother: "Behold, this child is set for the ruin and resurrection of many in Israel, and for a sign that shall be spoken against. And a sword <note>original: "gladius" (Latin). The Greek used "rhomphaia," a large Thracian sword, often used to signify a piercing grief or a sharp judgment.</note> shall pierce through your own soul." Nor does it seem any less doubtful to me how the same person is set for ruin and resurrection, and what the sign is that shall be spoken against; and thirdly, how a sword shall pierce Mary's soul. I believe, therefore, that the Lord is set for ruin and resurrection, not with some people falling and others rising: but rather that the evil within us should fall, and that which is better should rise. For the Lord's coming to earth has this power: to tear away the cravings of the body and to awaken the nature of the soul. When Paul says, "When I am weak, then I am strong," the same man is weak and strong: surely he is weak in the flesh, but strong in the spirit. Thus the Lord does not provide a cause for falling to some and rising to others: for those who fall clearly fall from a state in which they previously were. For he who does not believe does not stand in any way, and always creeps along with the serpent. He has no place from which to fall, because he always lies cast down through his lack of faith. The first blessing is that those things which stand in sin should fall and die, and then again...

<summary>This page presents a commentary by Basil the Great on the prophecy of Simeon, interpreting the "fall and resurrection of many" as the spiritual destruction of sin and the rising of the soul. It clarifies that Christ does not cause some to fail and others to succeed, but rather causes the "worse" part of every person to fall so their "better" part can rise.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the theological commentary on the prophecy of Simeon from the Gospel of Luke. Having previously established that Christ’s "falling and rising" refers to the death of our vices and the resurrection of our virtues, the author now interprets the "sign that is spoken against" as the Cross and the "sword" as the trial of faith during the Crucifixion.</meta>

# CHRONICON

...granting each of these states to us. Let our worse elements fall, so that the better may find the opportunity for <term>resurrection</term>. <note>The Greek term used here is "anastasis," which means rising up or resurrection.</note> Unless <term>fornication</term> falls, <term>self-control</term> does not rise; unless <term>irrationality</term> is crushed, the <term>rational</term> part within us will not flourish. This, then, is the meaning of "the fall and resurrection of many."

<margin>C</margin> As for the "sign that shall be spoken against," we have learned from Scripture that the <term>Cross</term> is specifically referred to as a "sign." <margin>R 486</margin> For Moses placed the serpent upon a sign—that is, upon a cross—which is a sign indicative of something miraculous and hidden; it was seen by the people, but understood only by those with an active and discerning mind. <note>This refers to the bronze serpent in the wilderness (Numbers 21), which healed those who looked at it; Christian tradition views this as a "type" or foreshadowing of Christ on the Cross.</note>

Because people never cease quarreling about the <term>Incarnation</term> <note>original: "enanthropesis," literally "becoming human"</note> of the Lord—some asserting he took a physical body, others that his coming was incorporeal; some that he had a body capable of suffering, others that his work through the body was fulfilled through a kind of illusion; <margin>D</margin> others saying he had an earthly body, and others a heavenly body; some that he existed before the ages, and others that he had his beginning from Mary—for this reason he is called "a sign spoken against."

By the "sword," he means the word that tests us, which judges our thoughts and reaches even to the division of soul and body, of joints and marrow, and the discerning of intentions. <note>This imagery is drawn from Hebrews 4:12, describing the power of the Word of God.</note> Since, therefore, at the time of the Passion, every soul was subjected to a kind of judgment, as it were, according to the voice of the Lord when he said: "All [of you shall be offended because of me]..."

R. 17. "but" omitted in PV. the second "the" omitted in P. 18. "and" omitted in R. 21. "was exceeding" in P.

[The following is a parallel translation of the Greek text above:]
...they shall rise through justice, as the knowledge of Christ grants both to us. Let the worse things therefore fall, that they may take the occasion of rising. Unless libido has first fallen, temperance shall not rise: unless the animal sense has first been crushed, the vigor of reason will not bloom in us. Thus, he was placed for the ruin and resurrection of many. As for the "sign which shall be contradicted": a sign is properly taken in sacred literature to mean the cross. For Moses proposed the serpent as a sign, that is, on a cross, which is an indication of something unusual and hidden, which is seen by everyone but understood only by those who are strong in intellect. Since, therefore, they do not cease to argue about the Lord’s becoming human—while some contend he assumed a body, others that he lived on earth without a body, some that he had a passible body, others that he fulfilled his coming in a phantom body; some that he assumed an earthly body, others a heavenly one, some that he was eternal by nature, others that he took his beginning from Mary—for this reason he is said to have been placed as a sign of contradiction. The "Rhomphaea" or sword, however, he calls the Word, which explores and discerns thoughts, and penetrates even to the division of soul and body, and to the joints and marrow of internal thoughts: for when he suffered, all were fluctuating in doubt at the voice of the Lord, when he said, *All shall be scandalized in me...* <note>The Latin text completes the sentence: "All you shall be offended because of me this night" (Matthew 26:31).</note>

# PASCHALE

...[all of you] will be made to stumble by me," Simeon prophesies concerning Mary herself: that while standing by the cross, seeing the things taking place <margin>P 205</margin> and hearing the voices—even after the testimony of the Archangel Gabriel, after the secret knowledge of the divine conception, and after the great display of miracles—there will occur a certain shaking <note>original: "salos," a term often used for the tossing of a ship or a storm at sea.</note> even within your own soul. For it was necessary for the Lord to taste death on behalf of everyone, and by becoming a <term>propitiation</term> <note>A sacrifice that brings reconciliation or atonement.</note> for the world, to justify all people by his own blood. Therefore, even you yourself, who were taught from above regarding the Lord, will be touched by a certain <term>distinction</term> <note>original: "diakrisis," here meaning a trial of discernment or a moment of doubt.</note>—that is, a sword—so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed. It will be beneficial, because after the <term>stumbling</term> <note>original: "skandalismon," referring to the crisis of faith at the Crucifixion.</note> that occurred at the cross of Christ for both the disciples and for Mary herself, a swift <margin>B</margin> healing from the Lord will follow, confirming their hearts in their faith. For in this way we know that Peter, after his stumbling, held even more firmly to his faith in Christ. Thus, human frailty was exposed so that the strength of the Lord might be taught, to whom be glory and dominion forever. Amen.

Then, for those wishing to know on which day of the week <margin>R 488</margin> the second of the month of February fell in the present year 5507 <note>In the Byzantine calendar, the year 5507 corresponds to 1 BC.</note>, we set down the single solar <term>epact</term> <note>A variable used in the "computus" (the calculation of the date of Easter) to track the difference between the solar and lunar calendars.</note>, and to this we join the days from the first of the month of April... <margin>C</margin>

...[to be offended]. Thus we see that Peter, after he suffered the scandal, kept a firmer faith in Christ. Therefore, human weakness was shown so that the power of the Lord might be taught, to whom is glory and empire forever. Amen.

15 in the current year 5,537 <note>Year 5537 of the Byzantine "Year of the World" (Anno Mundi) calendar</note>, taking the start from the 21st of the month of March—which is the 14th day of the first month of the moon <term>Nisan</term>—we process the 5,537 by [dividing by] 19 <note>19 refers to the Metonic cycle, used to calculate the phases of the moon</note>. 19 times 200 becomes 3,800; 19 times 90 becomes 1,710; 19 times 1 becomes 19.

<meta>This page continues the chronological and astronomical calculations for the life of Christ. # CHRONICLE

Then, wishing to know on what day the 14th of the first month of the moon <note>The 14th of Nisan, the day the Passover lamb was sacrificed</note> occurred, to the 5,535 years we add the fourth part, 1,384 <note>This "fourth part" represents the leap years accumulated over the period to synchronize the calendar</note>; this makes 6,920. Dividing these by 7: 7 times 900 makes 6,300; 7 times 80 makes 560; 7 times 8 makes 56; the remainder is 4 epacts <term>epact</term><note>The "epact" is the age of the moon in days on a specific date, used here to find the day of the week</note>. To these, add the 3 days before the luminaries and the 7 days from the 21st <margin>B</margin> of March itself; the total is 14. Dividing these by 7: take away 7, and 7 remains. We thus know that in the current year, the 14th of the first month of the moon occurred on the 27th of March, on a Saturday.

The 15th of the first month of the moon, which the divine Law calls the first day of Unleavened Bread <term>Azymorum</term><note>The feast of Matzah, or Unleavened Bread, beginning immediately after Passover</note>, occurred on the first day of the week—that is, the Lord's Day <note>Sunday</note>, which is the second day from the Sabbath. For it is the custom of the God-inspired Scripture to call every day that has a rest a "Sabbath." Therefore, it calls "Sabbath" not only the 14th of the first month of the moon when it falls on a Saturday, but also the 15th of the first <margin>C</margin> month of the moon, which is the first day of Unleavened Bread (even when it falls on the first day of the week), and the 21st of the same month, which is the seventh day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread and the seventh day of the week.

It seems to me that the divine Evangelist Luke refers to this Passover when he says: *It happened on the second-first Sabbath* <note>original Greek: σαββάτῳ δευτεροπρώτῳ (sabbato deuteroproto); a rare term found in Luke 6:1</note> *that Jesus and his disciples passed through the grain fields, and his disciples plucked the heads of grain and ate them.*

<column-break/>

<margin>v.</margin> If we wish also to know on which day the 14th of the month of the moon fell, we add the fourth part, 1,384, to 5,536 <note>The Latin translator uses 5536 while the Greek uses 5535, reflecting a variation in counting the current year</note>. These make 6,920. Divide these by 7: 7 in 900 makes 6,300; then 7 in 80 makes 560; again 7 in 8 makes 56. The remaining epacts are 4. To these, add 3 "pre-luminary" days and 7 from the 21st of the month of March; they make 14. From these, taking away 7, 7 will remain. Therefore, we conclude that in this present year, the 14th of the first month of the moon occurs on the 27th day of March, on a Saturday.

Truly, the 15th of the moon of the first month, which the divine law calls the first of the Unleavened Bread, occurs on the first day of the week—that is, Sunday—which is the second day from the Sabbath. For the Scripture inspired by God is accustomed to call each feast day a "Sabbath." Therefore, it calls it a Sabbath not only when the 14th of the lunar month occurs on a Saturday, but also the 15th of the first lunar month, which is the first day of Unleavened Bread, even when it occurs on the first day [of the week]; and also the 21st day of the same month, which is the seventh of the Feast of Unleavened Bread and the seventh day of the week. Furthermore, the divine Evangelist Luke seems to have indicated that Passover when he says: *But it happened on the Second-first Sabbath when Jesus passed through the sown fields with his disciples, who plucked the ears of grain so that they might eat.* He calls it the "Second-first Sabbath" not only because...

# PASCHAL CHRONICLE

He calls this Sabbath the "second-first" <term>deuteroproton</term><note>A rare and difficult term appearing in Luke 6:1. The author here explains it as a technical term for the first Sabbath occurring during the counting of the weeks toward Pentecost.</note>, not only because it was the seventh day of the week on which the first day of Unleavened Bread <term>Azymorum</term> occurred, but also because from this day the fifty days are numbered, and the feast is celebrated which the divine Law calls the "Feast of Weeks" <term>Hebdomadum</term><note>Known as Shavuot in Hebrew or Pentecost in Greek.</note>. <margin>R 502</margin> Therefore, since there were seven Sabbaths in this year of Pentecost—as it began on a <margin>5</margin><margin>D</margin> Sabbath and concluded on a Sabbath—it was the first Sabbath of those seven Sabbaths, and yet again the last of the whole count. For these reasons, wishing to indicate that during this Passover the Lord was passing through the grainfields with His disciples, the Evangelist <margin>10</margin> stated that on the "second-first" Sabbath, Jesus and His disciples passed through the grainfields.

The God-inspired Scripture clearly teaches that the divine Law calls the 14th day of the first lunar month "Passover," <margin>V 170</margin> while it names the 15th the "first of Unleavened Bread" and calls it a "Sabbath." Furthermore, it calls the 16th the first day of Pentecost. <margin>15</margin> For in <margin>P 212</margin> Leviticus it is written exactly as follows: "These are the feasts of the Lord, called holy, which you shall proclaim in their seasons. In the first month, on the 14th day of the month, between the evenings <note>original: "ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ἑσπερινῶν" — a literal translation of the Hebrew 'bein ha-arbayim', the time for sacrificing the lamb</note>, is the Passover to the Lord. <margin>20</margin> For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. And the first day shall be a holy convocation for you; you shall do no customary work, and you shall offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord for seven days..."

<margin>L.</margin> It is the first day on which the first of the Unleavened Bread was found, but also because from that day the days were counted and the feast was celebrated: which indeed the divine Law calls the Feast of Weeks. Since, therefore, seven Sabbaths exist in this year of Pentecost—as it takes its beginning from a Sabbath and ends on a Sabbath—it was the first of the seven Sabbaths and again the end of the whole number. On account of this, the Evangelist, wishing to show that the Lord passed through the crops during this Passover with His disciples, said that He passed through the crops on the "Second-first Sabbath" with His disciples.

Because the divine Law calls the 14th of the first lunar month "Passover" <note>Latin: Phase</note>, but the 15th the "first of the Unleavened Bread" and calls it a "Sabbath"; moreover, the 16th the "first day of the fifty" <note>Pentecost</note>, the God-inspired Scripture clearly teaches. You shall do no servile work." When, however, you have entered...

# CHRONICLE

<margin>B</margin>
...[from the time] of Tiberius Caesar and the beginning of the saving preaching <note>The start of Jesus's public ministry.</note>, which occurred in this present 15th year: 356 years.

<margin>R 510</margin>
Altogether, from Adam until the present 15th year of Tiberius Caesar—specifically until the 20th day of the month of March—the total is 5,537 full years.

After his baptism, the Lord spent another 3 years performing healings while living among his disciples. Luke makes this clear regarding these matters, saying that the Lord said because of Herod: *Go and tell that fox, "Behold, I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I reach my goal"* <note>Luke 13:32. The author interprets "today, tomorrow, and the third day" as three literal years of ministry.</note>. By these words, he signifies the three years. By saying "Today," he shows
<margin>C</margin>
that he revealed these things to Herod during the first year of his healings. John the Evangelist also shows this, identifying three years from Passover to Passover during the time of his healings.

Indiction 2 <term>Indiction: A 15-year cycle used in the Roman tax and dating system.</term>. Year 16. Under the consulship of Vennicius and Longinus.

In the present year 5538 from the creation of the world, which began on the 21st of the month of March according to the Romans, the Lord celebrated the second legal Passover after being baptized. Wishing to know on what day of the month the 14th day of the first lunar month <note>This refers to the "legal Passover" or Nisan 14 in the Jewish calendar.</note> occurred during this present year, we find that in the ninth year of the natural nineteen-year cycle <term>Greek: *enneakaidekaeteris*. A 19-year period used to synchronize the lunar and solar calendars.</term>, the added epacts <term>Greek: *epaktas*. The age of the moon on a specific date (usually March 22nd) used to calculate the date of Easter.</term> are 28. To these we add the 13 "pre-luminaries" <note>original: *pro ton phosteron*. These are technical astronomical variables used in the Paschal calculation.</note> and the 7 "pre-lunaries," as well as 11 days starting from the 21st of the month of March, and 15 days of April; the total is 74. We have thus determined that for the present year, the 14th day of the moon fell on the 15th of the month of April.

<margin>P 216</margin>
Furthermore, wishing to know the day of the week on which this 14th day fell, we find that in the 22nd year of the twenty-eight-year cycle <term>Greek: *oktokai-eikosat-eteris*. To these we join the 3 "pre-luminaries" and 11 from the 21st of the month of March, and 15 from April; the total is 34. Divide these by 7; seven times four is 28; the remainder is 6. # CHRONICON

...of this [Passover] he performed the symbolic supper, at the time when the sanctification of the unleavened bread and the preparation of the feast took place. He is found sharing with his disciples not a sacrificial victim nor unleavened bread, but bread and a cup. This was also when he washed the feet of the disciples, just as the <margin>C</margin> God-inspired words teach us—an act which was not performed according to the Mosaic <margin>5</margin> ordinance. For if he himself had not become—in place of the lamb that served as a type <note>original: "τύπον" (typon) — a symbol or foreshadowing in biblical interpretation.</note> and a shadow—the sacrifice that was long ago commanded by Moses to be sacrificed for those to come, the laws of Israel would not have passed <margin>R 518</margin> away. Instead, he would have been required to sacrifice a sheep and share it with his disciples, as he had done in previous <margin>10</margin> years, had the time not arrived for the fulfillment of the mystery concerning them. Thus, he brought the symbolic lamb to an end on the 22nd of the month of March according to the Romans, on the very day when the moon was on its 13th day, at the 5th hour of the night, as it dawned toward the 24th [day of the month], while Herod the Tetrarch was king, as *Luke* the Evange- <margin>15</margin> list <margin>D</margin> declares. ...it is gathered from this that he did not deliver to his disciples a sacrifice, nor *Unleavened Bread*, but bread and the chalice, and also when he washed the feet of the disciples, just as the God-inspired oracles teach, which indeed was not done according to the Mosaic precept. For if he had not been in the place of the symbolic lamb and sacrifice—since it had been prescribed of old by Moses for those who were to come that they should immolate a victim—he would by no means have stepped beyond the laws of Israel, but would have sacrificed a sheep and communicated it to his disciples, just as he had done in former years, unless the time for fulfilling these mysteries had been present. In the 20th year of the reign of Tiberius <note>Tiberius Caesar, the second Roman Emperor.</note>, beginning from the 21st of the month of March according to the Romans in this present 5th Indiction <note>The Indiction was a 15-year cycle used in the Roman Empire for tax and dating purposes.</note>, in the 25th year of the twenty-eight-year solar cycle and the 12th year of the nineteen-year lunar cycle <note>These astronomical cycles were used to ensure that Easter would always fall on a Sunday following the first full moon after the Spring Equinox.</note>, and under the aforementioned consuls; the 14th day of the first lunar month having been found to be on the 11th of April according to the Romans, on the sixth day of the week <note>Friday.</note>, as we find through the methods previously set forth, the holy Apostles first celebrated the Passover <note>original: "pascha." In this Christian context, it refers to the Easter celebration.</note> after the Lord’s Ascension into heaven. 

They celebrated His holy Resurrection on the 13th day of the month Xanthicus <note>Xanthicus was a month in the Macedonian calendar, here used as a synonym for April.</note>. They, therefore, having first performed the rite in this present year as has been said, handed it down to the holy churches of God to observe every year the 14th day of the first lunar month after the beginning of the day on which the spring equinox occurs—that is, the 21st of the month of March according to the Romans. 

<margin>R 536</margin> This account is free from any doubt: that the great luminaries <note>The sun and the moon.</note> were created three days after the foundation of the world <note>The author is harmonizing the Genesis creation account with the calendar, placing the creation of the sun and moon on the fourth day.</note>, and the mystical supper of the Lord with His disciples at the time of His Passion was performed three days before the holy Resurrection. 

<margin>V 181</margin> It was rightly decreed not to perform the Pascha before the 11th day before the Calends of April <note>March 22nd. The "Calends" was the first day of a Roman month; counting backward from April 1st makes this March 22nd.</note>, and that it is not permitted to celebrate [the feast] before this 11th day...

# CHRONICLE

<margin>P 226</margin> ...the first of April, nor should the feast of Passover <note>original: "pascha." While often translated as Passover in a Jewish context, in this Christian manuscript, it refers to the Resurrection festival, or Easter.</note> be celebrated after the 25th of April <note>original: "the 7th day before the Kalends of May."</note>. Thus, the rules must be applied to the designated days between the 22nd of March <note>original: "the 11th day before the Kalends of April."</note> and the 25th of April. And if the 14th day of the moon <note>This refers to the "Paschal Full Moon," the lunar date used to determine Easter.</note> should fall on a Sunday, we, the disciples of the Catholic Church of Christ, <margin>5</margin> celebrate the Passover on the following Sunday, so that we do not celebrate it alongside the Jews. But if the 14th day of the moon’s light should happen to fall on a Monday, or a Tuesday, or a Wednesday, or a Thursday, or a Friday, or a Saturday <note>The Greek text lists these as "second, third, fourth, fifth, preparation (Parasceve), or Sabbath."</note>—as has been stated previously—we Christians celebrate the Passover on the following Sunday, <margin>10</margin> essentially extending the age of the moon’s light for the sake of the Lord’s day.

<margin>B</margin> Now, there have been some who, regarding the festivals celebrated in the holy churches of God throughout the whole world, have dared to move not only their tongues but even their hands against them. They have not hesitated to find fault with the holy church of God on this point: namely, because it addresses the venerable <margin>15</margin> festival of the Resurrection of Christ our God from the dead as "Pascha," being ignorant, as it seems, of what is signified by this word. For that which in the Greek language is called "crossing over," "going out," or "passing over," <note>original: "diabasis," "ekbasis," and "hyperbasis."</note> is called *Phasoch*—that is, *Pascha*—in the Hebrew tongue. <margin>20</margin>

<margin>C</margin> Necessarily, therefore, the Church of God addresses not only the Passion of the Lord but also His Resurrection as "Pascha."

-> 7. Wednesday] or "fourth day." P reads "fourth." 12. "under the sun" P reads "under the sun's." 19. <-
-> "Phasoch"] P alone reads "Phasech." <-

---

<note>The following section is the Latin parallel text of the Greek above, provided by the original editor for scholars. It covers the same rules for the 14th moon and the etymology of Pascha.</note>

From the first of April to the 25th of April, on these designated days, the rule is to be taken. If the 14th moon falls on the Lord's day, we the disciples of the Catholic Church of Christ celebrate Pascha on the following Sunday, lest we celebrate it with the Jews. If, however, it falls by chance on the second, third, fourth, fifth day, or the Preparation, or the Sabbath, as was said above, we Christians hold the Pascha on the next following Sunday, the age of the moon being extended or prolonged specifically for the sake of the Lord's day.

There have not been wanting those who, while acting against the custom received by all the holy Churches of God under the sun in celebrating the Paschal feasts, dare to exercise not only their tongues but even their hands, not doubting to likewise rebuke the holy Church of God in this: that it has given the name of Pascha to the venerable festival of the Resurrection of Christ God from the dead. They themselves, it seems, are ignorant of what we understand by this vocabulary. For that which in the Greek tongue is called "passage," "exit," and "transmission," that very thing is called *Phasech*, or *Pascha*, in the idiom of the Hebrews.

Necessarily, therefore, the Church of God calls not only the Passion of the Lord, but also His Resurrection, "Pascha." Indeed, because of the Lord...

<header>PASCHAL MATTERS</header>

<margin>5</margin>...addresses it. For through the passion of the Lord and his resurrection, human nature has received a **passage**, an **exit**, and a **passing over** <note>The Greek terms used here—"diabasin," "ekbasin," and "hyperbasin"—all play on the etymological root of "Pascha" as a transition from death to life.</note> from the one who holds the power of death, and from death itself, and from Hades, and from corruption. For if the death of Christ bestowed this upon us, how much more so did his resurrection, when he rose from the dead as the **firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep**, <note>A reference to 1 Corinthians 15:20.</note> never <margin>R 536</margin> again destined to return to corruption. For **death no longer has dominion**, <margin>D</margin> according to the teaching of the divine Apostles. <note>A reference to Romans 6:9.</note>

<margin>10</margin> But it seems to me that those who have dared to accuse the Church in this matter have misunderstood the testimony from Leviticus <note>original: "Levitikon," referring to Leviticus 23:4-5.</note>, in which the Lawgiver <note>Moses</note> says: *And on the 14th day of the first month, between the evening times, is the Passover to the Lord. And on the 15th day of this month is the feast of Unleavened Bread to the Lord; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and the first day <margin>15</margin> shall be called holy for you; likewise the seventh day shall be called holy for you.* But the Lawgiver commands the Israelites to address only the 14th day as "Passover," since on <margin>P 227</margin> that very day, according to divine command, they sacrificed the lamb toward evening, and with its blood they anointed the doorposts and the lintels, and they ate the meat during that same night. And thus, at midnight, <margin>20</margin> as it is written, God passed through the land of Egypt to strike the firstborn of the Egyptians; but seeing the blood, he shielded the sons of Israel, passing over their doors...

<note>The following is the Latin translation of the Greek text provided in the original manuscript for scholars. It mirrors the content above.</note>

...His Passion and Resurrection, human nature received a passage, an exit, and a transition from him who has empire and power over death: into death itself, I say, and the lower world, and corruption. For if the death of Christ granted this to us, much more his Resurrection, when he rose from the dead, himself the firstfruits of those who sleep, never more to return to corruption. For death, according to the doctrine of the divine Apostles, no longer dominates.

Furthermore, those men seem to me to accuse the Church in this, while they dare to perversely interpret the testimony from Leviticus, where the Lawgiver says: *And on the fourteenth day of the first month at evening is the Phase <note>The Latin "Phase" is a transliteration of the Hebrew "Pesach" or Passover.</note> of the Lord. And on the fifteenth day of this month is the feast of Unleavened Bread to the Lord: for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and the first day, being called, shall be holy to you.* But the Lawgiver commands the Israelites to call only the 14th moon "Passover": since on that day, according to divine precept, they sacrificed the lamb towards evening, the flesh of which—after the thresholds and posts had first been anointed with its blood—they ate in that same night. And so, as it is written, the Lord passing through the land of Egypt in the middle of the night to kill the firstborn of the Egyptians, having seen the blood, covered the sons of Israel, passing through their doors and not permitting anyone of them to be struck by the exterminator.

**Vocabulary:** Passover, Resurrection, Leviticus, Unleavened Bread, Israelites, Egypt.

### CHRONICON

...indeed four years, but for three years Gaius reigned after him <note>Referring to the transition from Tiberius to Caligula.</note>, as Josephus <note>Titus Flavius Josephus, a 1st-century Romano-Jewish historian.</note> records.

Divine justice, it seems, pursued him not long after, as those who have written the Roman and Greek histories record, who also listed the Olympiads <note>The four-year periods used by Greeks to track time.</note> along with these events.

<margin>11th Indiction. 3rd Year. Under the consulship of Claudius Caesar and Cersianus.</margin>

<margin>V 185</margin> <margin>P 231</margin> Under the aforementioned consuls, Gaius Gallus <note>Better known as the Emperor Caligula.</note> was slain in the palace of Rome by his own guards <note>original: "σπαθαρίων" — literally "sword-bearers."</note> and chamberlains <note>original: "κουβικουλαρίων" — eunuch attendants of the imperial bedchamber.</note> according to the will of the Senate, at the age of 39.

In this first year of Claudius, Saint Stephen was martyred, and Paul was consenting to his execution. This was Stephen, the first martyr and first deacon of the New Testament, who had the great Paul (while he was still a zealot for the law) as his own murderer; who alone contended against the whole synagogue; who by the sight of his struggle caused the **Judge of the Games** <term>agonothetēs</term> <note>original: "ἀγωνοθέτην" — in ancient Greece, the official who presided over games and awarded prizes. For while all the Divine Scripture speaks of Him as sitting, this man saw Him standing; for the intensity of the struggle roused the Judge of the Games to witness the sight. Wherefore, being encouraged by Him to depart into that glory, he prayed for those who were stoning him, saying: *“Lord, do not hold this sin against them, but You Yourself receive my spirit.”* <note>A paraphrase of Acts 7:60 and 7:59.</note>

Behold, he also saw and proclaims the same things as the others: that Christ is in heaven as the leader of the second state <note>original: "δευτέρας καταστάσεως" — referring to the eternal order or the world to come.</note>, whom he entreats to receive him in that same place.

<margin>R 550</margin> In this fifth year of Claudius, Paul, having been previously ordained <note>original: "προχειροτονηθεὶς" / "ordinatus" — meaning appointed or chosen for his mission</note>, entered Great Antioch. Having learned about the scandal involving Saint Peter, he removed the cause of offense everywhere; he accepted and loved everyone, encouraging them all, just as the chroniclers Clement and Tatian <note>Clement of Alexandria and Tatian the Assyrian, second-century Christian authors</note> have written regarding this matter. He also traveled <margin>5</margin> to Cyprus, to Seleucia, and to other cities, teaching the word of God.

-> 3rd Indiction. 6th Year. Under the consulship of Asiaticus and Silanus. <- <note>This corresponds to approximately 46 AD.</note>

Under these consuls, Paul went up again to Jerusalem.
<margin>P 233</margin> It is concerning this ascent that he writes to the Galatians as <margin>10</margin> follows: "**After fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem.**" <note>Galatians 2:1</note> By saying "**Again**," it is clear that this is a different journey. When he says "**After 14 years**," it seems to me that he is counting the years of the apostles from the Ascension <note>The departure of Jesus to heaven</note>. For from the Ascension of the Lord until this ascent, fourteen years <margin>15</margin> and ten months of the apostolic era are completed. If we do not grant this calculation, the time from when he was baptized and regained his sight (as recorded in the **Acts**) would be found to be only four years. This is supported not only by what the **Acts** convey, but also by Josephus <note>Flavius Josephus, the Jewish historian</note>, who says that Herod <note>Herod Agrippa I</note> lived for three years of Claudius's reign, <margin>B</margin> and that immediately after the death of Herod, Paul and <margin>20</margin> Barnabas were called to their apostleship—that is, in the fourth year of Claudius.

He also came into Cyprus, and Seleucia, and into other cities, preaching the word of God.

<margin>5553.</margin> <margin>46. vi. Ind. iii. Under the consulship of Asiaticus and Silanus.</margin> <margin>2.</margin>
Under these consuls, Paul came again to Jerusalem: whence he writes to the Galatians about this journey thus: *After 14 years I went up again to Jerusalem.* For in saying *again*, it is evident that another journey of his is designated. But when he says, *after 14 years*, it seems to me that he himself numbers the years of the Apostles from the Ascension of Christ. For from the Ascension of the Lord until this journey, 14 years and 10 months of the Apostles are completed. If we do not allow this, the time from which he was baptized and received his sight, as the Acts contain, will be found to be 4 years. And this is gathered not only from the Acts, but also from Josephus, writing that Herod extended his life to the third year of Claudius: and immediately after the death of Herod, to the Apostleship...

## On Paul the Apostle. <margin>V 188</margin>

This is the great Paul the Apostle, the commander of the heavenly ranks, the one who has Christ speaking within himself, the <margin>10</margin> one who carries the marks of Christ in his body, the great <margin>R 554</margin> teacher of the church, the one who endures countless deaths every day for the sake of the church, the one who boasts in the Lord and in his own weaknesses, the one who has the grace of Christ bubbling up within him, <margin>P 235</margin> <margin>15</margin> the one who speaks in tongues to all the nations, the former persecutor but now the persecuted, the former sinner but now the recipient of mercy, the one who was caught up to the third heaven and again into paradise, the hearer of unspeakable words, the chosen judge of spiritual gifts, the great <term>canonarch</term> <note>original: κανονάρχης (kanonarchēs). In a church context, this is the official who leads the chanting or directs the "canon" of the liturgy.</note> and one who surpasses the <margin>20</margin> rest of the teachers of the church—Paul, whose greeting in all his letters serves as a sign: "Grace..."

...they predicted that God established a certain new state, and is establishing it, which he pre-announced through the mouth of all the Prophets. Nor did he declare that there would be another before this state, nor another after the one to come, but with all the Prophets and Apostles he pronounced these two alone: this one, I say, already present, and after this, that one which is to come.

## Concerning Saint Paul the Apostle.

This is that great Apostle Paul, leader of the heavenly troops, who has Christ speaking in himself, who carries the marks of Christ in his body, the great doctor of the Church, who sustains infinite deaths daily for the Church, who glories in the Lord and in his infirmities, who has the grace of Christ effervescing within him, who speaks in the languages of all nations, formerly a persecutor, but now having suffered persecution, formerly a sinner, but now having obtained mercy, caught up to the third heaven, and again into paradise, the hearer of secret words, the designated judge of spiritual graces, the great Canonarch, or <term>Precentor</term>, and surpassing the remaining doctors of the Church. Paul, whose greeting in all his Epistles is in place of a sign: "The Grace of the Lord." He always, in all his Epistles, as if already enjoying the second state of the blessed life, ex[pressed]...

<margin>D</margin>And if we should wish to collect all the Apostle’s <note>The "Apostle" refers to Saint Paul, whom the author credits with fourteen Epistles.</note> citations concerning this matter, we would find that nearly all fourteen of his letters speak throughout of this: that from this present <term>state (katastasis)<gloss>A technical term in this work referring to the "setup" or "condition" of the universe—first the mortal, then the immortal.</gloss></term> we are urged to run toward the future one. ...[from] God and his scriptures. Therefore, let the <margin>V 190</margin> <term>Greeks<gloss>The author uses "Greeks" (Hellenes) to refer to practitioners of traditional polytheism and classical philosophy, rather than an ethnic group.</gloss></term> be put to shame—those who suppose that the world is co-eternal with God, who preach the pre-existence of souls, and who reject the resurrection of bodies. He views the "pagan" idea of a spherical universe as a denial of the biblical "two-state" system, because a sphere suggests a cyclical, eternal motion rather than a linear movement toward a new kingdom.</note> For they say nothing different than what the Greeks proclaim: that the world is always thus, trapped in the corruption of bodies, and that there will never be another <term>state (katastasis)<gloss>The fixed condition or "setup" of the universe.</gloss></term>.

Let the <term>Manichaeans<gloss>Followers of Mani who believed the physical world and the human body were inherently evil creations of a dark god.</gloss></term> and the <term>Marcionites<gloss>A sect that rejected the Old Testament and the physical incarnation of Christ, viewing the creator of the world as a lesser, vengeful deity.</gloss></term> be put to <margin>C 10</margin> shame—those who cast off the flesh and declare it to be the handiwork of an evil principle. Let all those who reject our flesh be put to shame, as well as those who reject our souls—their fellow travelers—namely **Eutyches**, **Arius**, **Apollinaris**, and all their followers. <note>These figures represent various "heresies" regarding the nature of Christ: Arius denied his full divinity; Apollinaris denied he had a human mind; Eutyches was accused of denying his full humanity.</note> Let all the heretics be put to shame who do not confess **one God known and worshipped in three persons (hypostases)**, <margin>15</margin> who is the creator of heaven and earth, and who do not confess the resurrection of our flesh.

Let the **Samaritans** be put to shame, for they confess neither the resurrection of our flesh, nor angels, nor spirits. Let the unbelievers among the <margin>20</margin> **Jews** be put to shame—those who did not receive the Expected One <note>The Messiah, Jesus Christ.</note> and do not confess the Christian resurrection, but rather imagine a resurrection <margin>D</margin> just like the life we lead now, where people **marry and are given in marriage**. <note>A reference to Matthew 22:30, where Jesus clarifies that the resurrected do not marry.</note> But bravo! Bravo, and joy, and exultation to those who are truly Christians—to those...

# CHRONICLE

...the Lord having arrived, both he and his disciples—the evangelists and apostles—preached nothing other than these two, and only these two, states <note>The "two states" (Greek: *katastaseis*) refer to the present mortal world and the future immortal kingdom.</note>.

# PASCHALE
<note>Paschale: Likely referring to a "Paschal Letter," an annual letter sent by the Bishop of Alexandria to determine the date of Easter and provide theological instruction.</note>

...I doubled my affection for them. You inquired about that much-discussed saying that is passed around everywhere, from top to bottom, asking what its solution might be: *Everyone who kills Cain shall suffer sevenfold vengeance.* <note>original: "Πᾶς ὁ ἀποκτείνας Καϊν ἑπτὰ ἐκδικούμενα παραλύσει" — This refers to the difficult passage in Genesis 4:15 regarding the protection and punishment of Cain.</note> By asking this, you have commended yourself, <margin>10 C</margin> accurately observing what **Paul** handed down to **Timothy**: *“Give attention to reading”*; <note>original: "Τιμοθέου ὃ παρέδωκεν Παῦλος αὐτῷ, ἀκριβῶς φυλάσσοντι" — referring to 1 Timothy 4:13.</note> for <margin>R 570</margin> it is clear that you are devoted to reading. Despite this, you, "fervent in spirit," <note>original: "ζέων τῷ πνεύματι" — a quote from Romans 12:11.</note> have <margin>15</margin> brought us back from our cold state, like animals in hibernation, to a degree of wakefulness and vital energy.

The saying, then, can be understood quite simply, and it also allows for a more complex explanation. The simpler interpretation, which can provide an immediate meaning to anyone, is <margin>20 D</margin> this: that Cain must pay a sevenfold punishment for the things he did wrong. For it is not the way of a righteous judge to set equal punishments for equal crimes, but it is necessary that the one who initiates an evil must [suffer] with an addition...

...is to be hoped for them. After I saw those men coming to me with your letters, I doubled my feeling of love toward them. Therefore, that sentence, just as the words sound, can be explained by a simple understanding, and it can admit a varied meaning. The explanation which can be at hand for anyone is this: that the penalty must be doubled seven times for Cain on account of the crimes which he committed. For it is not the part of a fair judge to determine equal [punishment] for equal [crimes]...

### CHRONICON
<note>Chronicon: A "Chronicle" or historical record. In this context, it likely refers to a historical-theological commentary on the timeline of the Bible.</note>

...to pay what is owed, if he is to become better through punishments and make others more prudent by his example. Therefore, since it has been ordained that Cain should fulfill sevenfold the penalty for his sins, the one who kills him—it says—will release <note>original: "παραλύσει" — literally "to loosen" or "set free," suggesting that killing Cain would end his cycle of divine punishment prematurely.</note> for him that which was decreed against him <margin>5</margin> by the divine judgment. This is the meaning that presents itself at first reading.

<margin>P 242</margin> But since the mind is naturally inclined to search the depths of more diligent studies, it seeks the nature of justice: how is it fulfilled in the "sevenfold" and the "vengeance"? Are the sins seven in number, <margin>10</margin> or is there but one sin, yet seven punishments for that one? Scripture always limits the number of the forgiveness of sins to seven. "How often," it says, "shall my brother sin against me and I forgive him?"—this is Peter speaking to the Lord—"Up to seven times?" Then comes the response of the Lord: "I do not say to you up to seven times, <margin>15</margin> but up to seventy times seven." <note>original: "ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά" — Matthew 18:21–22. The number seven in the Bible often symbolizes completeness or perfection.</note> For the Lord did not move to another number, but <margin>B</margin> having multiplied the seven, he set the limit of forgiveness within it. And after seven years, the Hebrew was released from slavery. Seven weeks of years made the famous "Jubilee" <note>term: Jubilee (ἰωβήλαιον). From the Hebrew 'yobel,' it was a year of liberation every 50th year (7x7+1) where debts were cancelled and slaves freed.</note> for the ancients, in which the land kept the Sabbath. There was a cancellation of debts and a release <margin>20</margin> from slavery; a new life, as it were, was established from above in the <margin>R 572 V 194</margin> sevenfold number, with the old life receiving its completion in a certain way.

...to impose punishments for sins, but it is right that he should afflict the author of the crime with heavier punishments, so that he himself may be corrected and render the rest more hesitant to sin by his example. Therefore, because it had been decreed that Cain should pay a sevenfold penalty for his crimes, he who kills Cain—it says—will release <note>original: "solvet" — to loosen or pay out.</note> this very penalty decreed for him by the divine sentence. This is the first understanding of the reading that occurs in this place. But because the mind of the studious is accustomed to investigate the causes of things more deeply, it asks about justice: how is it satisfied through a sevenfold punishment? Is the crime sevenfold, or rather, is the fault simple and single, but the punishment sevenfold for one crime? The law of Divine Scripture always defines the number of the remission of sins by the number seven. "How often," he says, "shall my brother sin against me and I forgive him?" (these are the words of Peter to the Lord) "up to seven times?" Then the Lord responds: "I do not say to you seven times, but up to seventy times seven." Nor did the Lord pass to another number, but with the sevenfold multiplied, he remained within it and fixed it as the limit of forgiveness. And in the seventh year, the Hebrew was granted liberty. Seven weeks of years made exactly that most celebrated Jubilee of the ancients, in which the land rested, the names of debtors were cancelled, slavery was removed, and a new kind of life—as it were—began in the sevenfold number of fifty years (the prior and old life having been brought to an end)...

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the "sevenfold vengeance" of Cain. The previous page established that the number seven represents completeness and that divine punishment in this life is a form of mercy intended to prevent eternal suffering.</meta>

-># PASCHALE<-
<note>"Paschale" refers to a work concerning the calculation of Easter or a commentary on the Passover/Easter season, often part of a "Chronicon" or universal history.</note>

These things are symbols <note>original: "τύποι" (typoi) — patterns or prefigurations</note> of this present age, which circles around and passes us by through the cycle of seven days. It is in this age that the payment for more moderate sins takes place, according to the compassionate care of our good Master, so that we are not handed over to punishment <margin>5</margin> <margin>C</margin> in the infinite age to come. Therefore, the "sevenfold" exists because of our kinship with this world; for it is right that those who love the world should suffer loss most through the very things for which they chose to do evil. Whether you speak of the sins committed by Cain or the punishments decreed upon him by the Judge, you will find seven, and in this way you will not <margin>10</margin> miss the meaning.

Among the crimes dared by Cain, the **first sin** was envy at the preference shown to Abel. The **second** was the deceit with which he spoke to his brother, saying, "Let us go out into the field." The **third** was the murder itself. The **fourth** was the intensification of the evil, for it was the murder of a brother, which increased the gravity of the act. The **fifth** <margin>D</margin> <margin>5</margin> was that Cain was the first murderer, leaving a wicked example for the rest of life to follow. The **sixth** was the wrongdoing of causing grief to his parents. The **seventh** was that he lied to God; for when he was asked, "Where is your brother Abel?" he said, "I do not know." Therefore, he discharged <note>original: "παρέλυσεν" — literally "to loosen" or "undo," here meaning the cancellation of the debt of punishment</note> seven avenged things when Cain was killed.

For since the Lord said, "Cursed is the ground, which opened..."

<margin>P 243</margin>...[the earth opened its mouth] to receive the blood of your brother, and you shall be groaning and trembling upon the earth. Cain said, *“If You cast me out today from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from Your face, and I shall be groaning and trembling on the earth, then anyone who finds me will kill me.”* To this, the Lord said, <margin>5</margin> *“Not so; anyone who kills Cain shall suffer a sevenfold vengeance.”* <note>original: "ἑπτὰ ἐκδικούμενα" (hepta ekdikoumena) — seven things to be avenged or seven penalties.</note> For since Cain thought he was easy prey for anyone because he no longer had security from the earth—since the earth was cursed because of him—and because he was desolated of help from God, who was angry at the murder, he felt that no help remained for him from either earth or heaven. <margin>10</margin> *“It will be,”* he said, <margin>B</margin> *“that everyone who finds me will kill me.”* The Word <note>The "Logos" or the voice of God.</note> corrects his error by saying, <margin>R 574</margin> *“Not so,”* which means: you shall not be put to death. But he [Cain] not only hides his wound, but adds another to it, joining a lie to the murder: *“I do not know; am I my brother’s keeper?”* From this point on, the punishments are numbered. <margin>15</margin> **The earth is cursed because of you.** This is the first punishment. **You shall work the earth.** This is the second. For a certain unutterable necessity was joined to him, driving him to the labor of the earth, so that even if he wished, he was not permitted to rest; instead, he was always forced to toil away on his enemy, the earth, which he himself had made cursed by defiling it with a brother’s <margin>20</margin> blood. <margin>C</margin> For it is a terrible punishment to live among those who hate you...

But he not only covers his sore, but adds another to the slaughter while he concocts a lie and says: *“I do not know, am I my brother's keeper?”* From this point God begins to number the penalties. **The earth shall be cursed by you.** The first punishment. **Work the earth.** This is the second penalty. For a certain inexplicable necessity was attached to him, which so urged him to the work that he was not permitted to take any part of rest even if he wanted it, but it pressed upon him most assiduously; the earth was to him infested and hostile, which he had made execrable for himself when he polluted it with brotherly blood. For it is a bitter kind of punishment to live with those who hate you, and [to have] a domestic enemy...

It identifies the first two punishments as the cursing of the earth and the forced, restless labor Cain must perform on that hostile land.</summary>

# CHRONICON PASCHALE 455

...lifestyle, to have an enemy living in the same house, and to harbor an unceasing hatred. <margin>V 195</margin> **You shall work the earth, that is,** you shall be so strained by agricultural labors that you will have no time to rest, day or night, from your toil. Instead, you will be driven to your tasks by a necessity more harsh than any master, <margin>5</margin> **and it shall no longer yield its strength to you.** <note>original: "καὶ οὐ προσθήσει δοῦναι τὴν ἰσχὺν αὐτῆς" (kai ou prosthēsei dounai tēn ischyn autēs). This implies the soil will be intentionally sterile for him.</note> For even if unceasing labor produced some fruit, the toil itself would be a significant torment for one who is always strained and exhausted. But since the labor is both unceasing and the hardship of the earth is fruitless, it results in the utter futility of his efforts. <margin>D</margin> **You shall be groaning and trembling** <margin>10</margin> **upon the earth.** <note>In the Greek Septuagint version used by the author, Cain is cursed to "groan and tremble" (stenōn kai tremōn), whereas most modern English Bibles, following the Hebrew, say "a fugitive and a wanderer."</note> He added two more punishments to the previous three: a continuous groaning and a trembling of the body, because the limbs no longer possess the stability that comes from strength. Since he used his bodily power for evil, his physical vigor was taken away, so that he was shaken and convulsed. He was no longer able to easily bring bread <margin>15</margin> to his mouth, nor to carry a drink; after his unholy deed, his wicked hand was no longer permitted to serve even the necessary needs of his own body. There is yet another punishment, <margin>P 244</margin> which Cain himself revealed when he said, **"If You cast me out now from the face of the earth, then I shall be hidden from Your face."** <margin>20</margin> To those who are wise, the heaviest punishment is separation from God. **"And it shall be," he says, "that everyone who finds me will kill me."** He infers what will follow from the preceding punishments.

...to retain, and to nourish an eternal hatred. **Work the earth, that is**, never at any time slacken from the sweat of cultivating and digging the earth, so that you may breathe from labor neither by night nor by day. Instead, driven by an extreme necessity that surpasses all servile slavery, you shall always be urged to work, yet you shall not make the earth any better through constant cultivation. For although continuous work usually has a fruit of labor, nevertheless the toil itself brings immense trouble and torment to one who is always stretched thin, always occupied, and never ceasing from work. But you, with your immense labor, will gain nothing, nor will you achieve anything worth the effort, nor will you carry back any fruit. Furthermore, **you shall be groaning and trembling upon the earth.** He added two other punishments to the three: constant sighs and a trembling of the body, the firmness of the limbs—which they received from strength or vigor—having been lost. For when he had abused the strength of his body, the muscle failed him, so that he trembled and was shaken by a certain constant trepidation, such that he could neither safely move food to his mouth nor carry a cup without trembling; his impious hand, after the impious and parricidal act, withdrew its use for the necessary functions of the body. Another punishment is that which Cain betrayed when he said: **"If you eject me today from the face of the earth, I shall be hidden from your face."** This is the most severe penalty to the prudent: rejection from the face and sight of God. **"And it will be," he said, "that everyone who finds me will kill me."** He guesses from the prior punishments those that will follow. If you eject me from the face of the earth, if from the face...

# CHRONICON PASCHALE 456

<margin>R 576</margin> ...of those who went before: "If I am cast out from the earth, and if I shall be hidden from your face, it follows that I will be killed by anyone." <note>original: "Εἰ ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐκβέβλημαι... ἀναιρεῖσθαι" (Ei apo tēs gēs ekbeblēmai... anaireisthai). Cain expresses his fear that being an outcast makes him prey for anyone he encounters.</note> What then does the Lord say? "Not so," but He set a mark upon him. This is the **seventh punishment**: that the punishment itself should not be hidden, but <margin>B</margin> rather proclaimed to everyone by a clear sign, showing that this man is the author of unholy deeds. Indeed, to one who reasons correctly, shame is the heaviest of punishments. We have learned this regarding the Final Judgment: that some shall rise to eternal life, and others to eternal shame and reproach. <note>A reference to the biblical Book of Daniel 12:2, connecting Cain's earthly shame to the spiritual concept of eternal disgrace.</note>

Following this is a related question concerning the words spoken by Lamech to his wives: **"I have killed a man for my wounding, and a youth for my bruising."** <note>Genesis 4:23. Lamech was the great-great-great-grandson of Cain.</note> There is a difference between a "wound" and a "bruise," just as there is a difference between a "man" and a "youth." If Cain was avenged sevenfold, but Lamech **seventy times seven**—meaning he must endure four hundred and ninety punishments—is this not <margin>C</margin> just? God’s judgment upon Cain was just in assigning him seven punishments. For Cain had not learned how to murder from anyone else, nor had he seen a murderer suffering punishment.

"But I," <insert>Lamech says</insert>, "having before my eyes the man who groans and trembles, and seeing the magnitude of God’s wrath, did not learn wisdom from his example. Therefore, I am worthy of receiving four hundred and ninety punishments." <note>Lamech argues that his sin is greater than Cain's because he ignored the visible warning of Cain's suffering.</note> Some, however, have pursued a different explanation, one not out of harmony with the Church...

## 212th Olympiad.

<margin>B V 197</margin> Vespasian reigned as the seventh emperor of the Romans for 9 years, 11 months, and 22 days, after the army crowned him. Total years: 5,586. <note>This high number refers to the "Annus Mundi" or years since the creation of the world according to the chronicler's calculations.</note> 11th Indiction. 1st year of the reign. In the consulship of Galba and Titus Rufus. <note>While Galba was consul in 69 AD, "Titus Rufus" is likely a scribal error for Titus Vinius, Galba's co-consul.</note>

Under these consuls, the bodies of the holy apostles <note>Referring to Peter and Paul</note> were given over for burial by order of Emperor Vespasian; for he was commanded in a vision to give the bodies of the holy apostles over for burial.

<margin>R 582</margin> In the same year, the holy apostle James, the Patriarch of Jerusalem—whom Saint Peter had enthroned in his own place when he departed for Rome—passed away. Symeon, also known as Simon, received the office of the bishopric of Jerusalem and became Patriarch.

<margin>C</margin> Under these same consuls, Nicomedia, the great metropolis of Bithynia, suffered from <term>divine wrath</term> <note>original: θεομηνίας (theomenia). This term was commonly used by Byzantine chroniclers to describe natural disasters, particularly earthquakes, viewed as acts of God.</note>.

In this year, King Agrippa, the brother of Berenice, died after reigning 26 years; and thereafter, Vespasian dissolved the kingdom of the foreigners, Herod and Agrippa. <note>Agrippa II was the last ruler of the Herodian dynasty; after his death, his territories were fully integrated into the Roman province of Syria.</note>

## 212th Olympiad.

<margin>5585</margin> Vespasian reigned as the seventh emperor of the Romans for 9 years, having been chosen by the army and presented with the diadem. The years are totaled as 5,586.

69 AD. 1st Year. 11th Indiction. In the consulship of Galba and Titus Rufus. 1st year of the 212th Olympiad.

Under these same consuls, the bodies of the holy Apostles were placed in a tomb by the decree of Emperor Vespasian; for he was ordered through a vision to entrust the bodies of the holy Apostles to the earth.

In this same year, the holy apostle James, the Patriarch of Jerusalem—whom Saint Peter had appointed as Bishop in his place—died while traveling to Rome, and Symeon, who was also called Simon, received the dignity of the Bishopric of Jerusalem and was made Patriarch.

Under the same consuls, Nicomedia, the great metropolis of Bithynia, [suffered] from divine wrath...

In this year King Agrippa, the son of Berenice <note>The Latin text here says "son," but the Greek text and historical fact identify him as her brother.</note>, died after he had reigned for 26 years. At the same time, Vespasian destroyed the kingdom of the foreigners Herod and Agrippa.

In the thirty-ninth year after the Lord’s ascension into heaven, Titus, the son of Vespasian, took possession of Judea and Jerusalem. Titus laid waste to all the provinces of Judea.

...thus: because the Jews crucified Christ during the feast, they all perished during their own feast. As the fortieth year since the Lord’s ascension into heaven began, in the second year of Vespasian, the leaders of the Jews ceased to exist entirely, for their final destruction overtook them.

The entire span of time is calculated up to the second year of Vespasian and the final capture of Jerusalem: from the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar himself and the beginning of the saving preaching <note>The start of Jesus's public ministry.</note> it is forty-two years; from the sixth year of Darius son of Hystaspes, when the temple happened to be rebuilt for the second time <margin>P 248</margin>—that is, from the second year of the 63rd Olympiad <note>A four-year period used by Greeks to reckon time; the 63rd Olympiad began around 528 BC.</note>—up to this present second year of Vespasian, it is 597 years; and from its first construction <note>original: ἐπισκευῆς (episkeuēs)</note> under Solomon, it is 1,103 years.

<meta>This page continues the chronology of Emperor Hadrian’s reign, focusing specifically on his response to the Jewish revolt and the subsequent Roman reconstruction of Jerusalem as a pagan city.</meta>

# CHRONICON

<margin>V 203</margin> 1st Indiction. 3rd year. Under the consulship of Aelius Hadrian Augustus (for the 2nd time) and Rusticius.

During these consulships, when the Jews had risen in revolt, Hadrian came to Jerusalem. He took the Jews captive and, traveling to the place called Terebinth <note>original: Τερέβινθον (Terebinthon); this refers to the site of Mamre near Hebron, famous for an ancient sacred tree. It was a major site for fairs and markets in antiquity.</note>, he established a public fair. There, he sold the captives for the price of a horse’s ration of feed <note>This indicates the massive surplus of slaves following the war, making human life tragically cheap.</note>. 
<margin>P 254</margin> The remaining captives he took to Gaza, where he also established a fair and sold them. To this day, that fair is called the "Hadrianic Fair."

After demolishing the Temple of the Jews in Jerusalem, he built two public baths, a theater, a triple-chambered building <note>original: τρικάμαρον (trikamaron); likely a vaulted structure with three sections.</note>, a four-nymph fountain <note>original: τετράνυμφον (tetranymphon); a monumental fountain-house dedicated to nymphs, typically square or four-sided.</note>, and a twelve-gate structure <note>original: δωδεκάπυλον (dodekapylon)</note> which was formerly called the "Steps" <note>original: ἀναβαθμοὶ (anabathmoi); referring to the monumental staircases that once led to the Jewish Temple.</note>. He also built the *Kodra* <note>original: κόδραν; likely a phonetic spelling of the Latin *quadra*, referring to a square city block or a specific plaza.</note>. He divided the city into seven districts <note>original: ἄμφοδα (amphoda); city quarters or neighborhoods.</note> and appointed his own men as <term>amphodarchs</term> <note>district chiefs or neighborhood administrators.</note>, assigning one district to each chief. Even today, each district is named after its original chief. He also gave the city his own name, calling it **Aelia**, because he was named Aelius Hadrian.
<margin>B</margin> 
2nd Indiction. 4th year. Under the consulship of Severus and Fulcus.

->**225th Olympiad**<-

<margin>A. C. 119</margin> <margin>[Ol. Iph.] III.</margin> 1st Indiction. Under the consulship of Aelius Hadrian Augustus (II) and Rusticius. <margin>3.</margin>

During these consulships, with the Jews rioting, Hadrian came to Jerusalem. Having made the Jews captives, he set out for Terebinth, as the city is called, and instituted public nundinae <note>nundinae: Roman market days or trade fairs.</note> where he sold them, valued at the price of a horse's fodder. He led the rest to Gaza and, having established a market there, he sold them off; from this, those markets are called "Hadrianic" to this day. 

Then, having overturned the Temple of Jerusalem, he founded two public baths, a theater, a Triple-Chamber, a Four-Nymph Fountain, a Twelve-Gate structure (which they formerly called the *Anabathmos* or "steps"), and the *Codra*. He further divided the city into seven districts and put in charge of them selected men called <term>Vicomagistri</term> <note>Vicomagistri: Latin for "masters of the neighborhood," officials who oversaw local shrines and administrative tasks.</note>, assigning a district to each master. From these men, the individual districts retain their names to this day. He also imposed his own name on the city, calling it **Aelia**, since he was called Aelius Hadrian.

<margin>120. IV.</margin> 2nd Indiction. Under the consulship of Severus and Fulcus. <margin>4.</margin>

->**225th Olympiad**<-

<margin>121. V.</margin> 3rd Indiction. Under the consulship of Severus (II) and Augurinus. <margin>1. 225.</margin>
